name: OBW Vixen's World Championship
epitaph: Debuted 1 February 2012 on the first night of Wednesday Night Catfight, the federation's own Vixens-only brand, when Cream Stylez beat Jade Mystique in a match its ledger records as merging the OBW Divas Championship and the Execution Woman's Championship into one belt. Ten reigns follow in fourteen months, none of them longer than Mystique's own 92 days, and the belt travels through pay-per-views the federation named Heart of Wrestling, Alcatraz Aggression, Wheel of Torture, Last Man Standing and Xtreme Xmas. The ledger's last word is Ayden Starr-Malice's second reign, won in a falls-count-anywhere five-way at Heart of Wrestling 2013 and still running at 63 days when the record stops.

name: OBW Vixen's Television Championship
epitaph: Debuted 28 February 2012 at the federation's own Big Shot pay-per-view, where Kitten beat three others in a sudden-death four-way to become the first champion. Its own article and its own ledger disagree about the belt's size — the prose says six reigns shared between five wrestlers, the table lists ten across nine — and both are recorded here rather than resolved. Leda's 82 days is the longest reign on it; Mahlia won hers in what the ledger calls the first ever Vixens Lockdown.

name: OBW Vixen Tag Team Championships
epitaph: The oldest belt the federation's own record dates, crowned 2 July 2011 on Friday Night Storm and defended almost entirely on that brand. Ashanti and Paisley held it three separate times across five months. The Lace Twins took it in a three-way in April 2012 and held it 122 days, the longest reign on the ledger — and lost it not in a match but to a firing, the belt handed to Snickers and Jade Mystique at Violent Voting once the twins were gone.

name: OBW Championship
notes: Ledger source: promotions/obw/archive/obw-champions.html; reign chain also drawn from promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html and promotions/obw/archive/james-parker.html.
epitaph: OBW's own men's flagship singles title, tracked only through incidental mentions on other wrestlers' bios and the federation's own last-touched champions list rather than a dedicated title-history page. Sidster is the earliest attested holder, backed by the newly formed stable the Flock to a defense at Rebirth (30 April 2012); the record does not say when his reign began or ended. Super Krmi held the belt next, by the time Chad Bowens dethroned him on the Storm episode after Storm's 54th — a reign Bowens's own bio credits him with holding twice in total, though only this one surfaces by name in the surviving record. Bowens lost the title the same night to a Money in the Bank-style cash-in by Ice, whose own caption calls it his only reign. How or when Ice lost the belt is not recorded; the corpus resumes the men's title story in early 2013 with Punisher already the Storm-side rival of Execution's own M-Star, and the wiki's own champions list, last touched 21 February 2014, still names Punisher, leader of the stable the Prophecy, as champion.

name: OBW World Heavyweight Championship
notes: Ledger source: promotions/obw/archive/obw-champions.html; reign chain also drawn from promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html and promotions/obw/archive/mvp-lux.html. Distinct from the wing's other men's flagship, the OBW Championship (Sidster/Krmi/Bowens/Ice/Punisher lineage), which is reconstructed separately.
epitaph: OBW's second men's flagship singles title, attested only through incidental mentions on other wrestlers' own bios and the federation's own last-touched champions list; no dedicated title-history page survives for it, unlike the Vixens belts. MVP Lux is the earliest attested holder, named only as the champion Chad Bowens dethroned; the record does not say how or when Lux won it, though it does record him earning an open-ended championship opportunity in an Elimination Chamber match at Death Trap (30 July 2012). Bowens won the title from Lux at an Execution television taping ("Execution 86", by his own account 25 June 2013), with help from an outside beatdown of Lux by four other wrestlers, but was forced to vacate it after an in-storyline injury. How or when the vacancy was filled is not recorded; the wiki's own champions list, last touched 21 February 2014, names M-Star as champion by then.
